measurement: peak frequency, mean, Chyulu Hills (n = 4 bats)
method: hand-released bats recorded in real time outside cave entrances with a handheld ultrasound detector (Pettersson D1000X, 384 kHz sampling, 16 bit); 512-point FFT, Hanning window; ten best signal-to-noise calls measured per bat in Kaleidoscope
conditions: Free-flying bats after hand release outside lava-tube day roosts, Chyulu Hills, Kenya; n = 4 bats with ten calls each (16 bats in the whole study, three sites). Table 1 prints means (+/- S.E.) with observed ranges in parentheses; the table has no caption or footnote, the S.E. is stated in the text ('Means (+/-S.E.) are presented, with observed ranges in parentheses'). Table 1 column header: 'Otomops harrisoni Chyulu Hills (n = 4)'. The row quoted also holds the Mt Suswa / Chyulu Hills counterpart and an 'Otomops sp.' Musanze, Rwanda column (n = 6); only the Chyulu Hills column is filed here. Chyulu Hills (first) Calls were assigned to species by association: the Methods say calls could not be recorded from genetically sampled bats, which were kept as museum vouchers, and the Discussion says vocalizing bats 'were only identified by association'; the Chyulu Hills roost is the one where only O. harrisoni were genotyped. Peak frequency differed significantly among cave sites (Chyulu Hills higher than Mt Suswa and Musanze); call duration did not differ significantly among sites (P > 0.05). Sex and age not stated.
